anchors.phrase: Now let's write the optimal solution.
anchors.purpose: Empty live code surface appears.

anchors.phrase: First, store the array length in n,
anchors.purpose: Type line 1: n = len(nums)

anchors.phrase: then set i to n -2.
anchors.purpose: Type line 2: i = n - 2

anchors.phrase: We move i left.
anchors.purpose: Motivation for while loop and i -= 1

anchors.phrase: While i is valid, and nums at i is greater than or equal to nums at i plus 1.
anchors.purpose: Type line 3: while i >= 0 and nums[i] >= nums[i + 1]: and line 4: i -= 1

anchors.phrase: When this loop stops, either we found the pivot, or no pivot exists.
anchors.purpose: Semantic proof: two possible exit states for i (i >= 0 or i == -1)

anchors.phrase: If i is still greater than or equal to 0, we have a valid pivot.
anchors.purpose: Type line 5: if i >= 0:

anchors.phrase: Now set j to n minus 1.
anchors.purpose: Type line 6:     j = n - 1

anchors.phrase: Move j left,
anchors.purpose: Motivation for successor loop body: j -= 1

anchors.phrase: while nums at j is less than or equal to nums at i.
anchors.purpose: Type line 7:     while nums[j] <= nums[i]: and line 8:         j -= 1

anchors.phrase: When that loop stops, j is the first value from the right. That is strictly greater than the pivot.
anchors.purpose: Semantic proof: j is guaranteed smallest value strictly larger than pivot

anchors.phrase: Now swap nums at i with nums at j.
anchors.purpose: Type line 9:     nums[i], nums[j] = nums[j], nums[i]

anchors.phrase: Next, set left to i plus 1,
anchors.purpose: Type line 10: left = i + 1

anchors.phrase: and right to n minus 1.
anchors.purpose: Type line 11: right = n - 1

anchors.phrase: While left is smaller than right,
anchors.purpose: Type line 12: while left < right:

anchors.phrase: swap nums at left with nums at right,
anchors.purpose: Type line 13:     nums[left], nums[right] = nums[right], nums[left]

anchors.phrase: then move left forward
anchors.purpose: Type line 14:     left += 1

anchors.phrase: and right backward.
anchors.purpose: Type line 15:     right -= 1

anchors.phrase: This reverses the suffix in place.
anchors.purpose: Semantic proof: suffix [left..right] reversed O(K) in-place

anchors.phrase: If no pivot was found, i becomes minus 1.
anchors.purpose: Docked proof: edge case [5, 4, 3, 2, 1], i drops to -1

anchors.phrase: Then the swap block is skipped,
anchors.purpose: Highlight: if i >= 0: block is completely skipped

anchors.phrase: and left becomes 0 automatically.
anchors.purpose: Evaluate: left = i + 1 = -1 + 1 = 0 automatically!

anchors.phrase: So the same reverse loop reverses the whole array.
anchors.purpose: Proof: reverse [0..n-1] turns entire array into ascending order

anchors.phrase: That turns the largest permutation into the smallest permutation.
anchors.purpose: Wraparound guarantee: [5, 4, 3, 2, 1] -> [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]

anchors.phrase: The important part is not memorizing these lines.
anchors.purpose: Philosophy transition: 3 universal algorithmic invariants

anchors.phrase: Each line follows the same reasoning. Find the rightmost place that can increase.
anchors.purpose: Invariant 1 card: Find rightmost non-maximal element (pivot)

anchors.phrase: Make the smallest increase.
anchors.purpose: Invariant 2 card: Swap with next greater element (successor)

anchors.phrase: Then minimize the suffix.
anchors.purpose: Invariant 3 card: Reverse descending suffix to minimal ascending
